# obix-runtime-browser

> Previous name: `@obinexusltd/obix-runtime-browser` — OBIX packages are named without an npm scope since decision D-102 (2026-09-29); the package, its version and its exports are unchanged.

The browser entry of OBIX's native runtime: createObixApp(ir, options) makes an application of a root component of canonical DOP IR, and mounts it in a page. No Vue, no React. Phase 6 (docs/recovery/native-runtime.md).

<!-- obix-release:begin — generated by scripts/release/prepare.mjs; edit the text above this line -->

## Installation

```bash
npm install obix-runtime-browser
```

## Basic usage

```js
import { ObixRuntimeError, createObixApp } from 'obix-runtime-browser';
```

## API surface

- `obix-runtime-browser` — 2 value exports: `ObixRuntimeError`, `createObixApp`
- Type declarations: `./dist/index.d.ts` (and a declaration next to every JS entry point).

## Architecture role

`obix-runtime-browser` is a **public building block**: the umbrella `obix` depends on it and re-exports its stable API, so applications normally reach it through `obix`; it can also be installed on its own.

The architecture of OBIX — the package families and which packages are public API — is indexed in the umbrella: [docs/architecture.md](https://github.com/obinexus/obix/blob/main/docs/architecture.md).

## Package relationships

- Depends on (OBIX): [`obix-runtime-reactivity`](https://github.com/obinexus/obix-runtime-reactivity), [`obix-runtime-dom`](https://github.com/obinexus/obix-runtime-dom), [`obix-runtime-component`](https://github.com/obinexus/obix-runtime-component).
- Used by (OBIX): [`obix`](https://github.com/obinexus/obix).

## Testing

- 1 test file ships in the npm package (`test/`): the evidence of the package's contract, published so that its verification can be inspected — not runtime code (no entry point reaches it).
- **Standalone**: 1 of 1 — it reads nothing outside the package.
- Run them with `npm test` (`node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`) in the OBIX monorepo, which provides the test tooling (Node's test runner, TypeScript) and the harness.
